values: The nominated authorization clause for Outfall 001 in Part I Section A
The immediately following sentence linking 'Such discharges' to the Outfall 001 limitations and monitoring table
Federal FY2025 monitoring periods and any evidence of which discharge types were occurring at Outfall 001

grounding.excerpt_span: authorized to discharge storm runoffs from storage and production areas, once-through cooling water, cleaning water, and Artesian well water from Outfalls 001
Such discharges shall be limited and monitored by the permittee as specified below (1)

grounding.note: No packet observation supplies Federal FY2025 monitoring periods or discharge-type occurrence evidence for Outfall 001

rationale: The packet partially addresses the interpretive linkage between the Outfall 001 authorization clause and the limitations table: the authorization enumerates four discharge categories, and the immediately following sentence uses 'Such discharges' to attach the monitoring/limitations table to those authorized categories rather than to Outfall 001 generically. That textual linkage is suggestive of discharge-type conditioning but, standing alone, does not establish the operational applicability question framed for Federal FY2025 across purposes A, B, and C. The obligation's third value—Federal FY2025 monitoring periods and evidence of which discharge types were occurring at Outfall 001—is absent from the packet, and the packet itself flags that it may be evidence-insufficient. Without that operational evidence, neither ACCEPT (that limitations and monitoring apply only when one or more enumerated discharge types is occurring throughout the relevant FY2025 periods) nor REJECT (that they apply to any Outfall 001 discharge without discharge-type conditioning) can be grounded to the burden required for semantic closure. REJECT is especially unsupported because the available permit text does not establish unconditional applicability, and absent operational records cannot be converted into negative closure. Per P5, unsupported uncertainty is preferred to unsupported semantic closure.
